items.text: Telltale's complaint database showed 31 confirmed conductor fractures among about 22,000 ArcLine AL-4120 leads shipped (about 0.14 percent) as of the 2025 review. Engineering had not yet confirmed whether the rate stayed within the labeled range.

A 2020 internal note from a Telltale field engineer said returned AL-4120 leads showed wear from repeated bending near the pocket and suggested the design be revisited. As of October 2025 it had not been produced in discovery in a prior AL-4120 matter, and it is regarded as a sensitive document.

A 2021 Telltale trend report followed an internal quality inquiry into returned-lead fractures, called the Larkspur review. Plaintiffs may argue the report put Telltale on notice of a rising fracture rate and required updated warnings.
The AL-4120 instructions for use warn against medial subclavian puncture and describe lateral venous access as the preferred approach.

Telltale settlement authority process: after the firm assesses a claim, it sends the General Counsel an assessment and recommended range. Authority above $500,000 needs sign-off from the CFO, Cormac Brightwater.

Telltale's working budget assumption on a product liability case was resolution or trial for under $500,000 in fees and costs combined, with an explanation wanted if the estimate goes higher. Because Telltale is in a regulatory inspection tied to its next-generation lead, it asks the firm to avoid public filings that characterize failure rates beyond what the case requires.
